title: Maintenance Kept and the Comfort Club Maintained Repair Amount
content:
Comfort Club Maintenance Agreements tie the extent of a covered repair to whether the agreement's maintenance has been kept. The test is the number of completed cooling or heating tune-ups on the agreement dated within the 12 months before the date of handling. Whole-home visits, forfeited visits and visits not yet performed do not count.

## Maintenance rule
| Completed cooling or heating tune-ups in the 12 months before the date of handling | Maintained repair amount |
|---|---|
| None | The repair parts only: the repair parts lines less the tier's member repair discount percentage, rounded to the cent half up. The labor stays with the member. |
| Exactly one | The discounted repair amount less the tier's tune-up retail value (109.00 USD on every Comfort Club tier) for the maintenance visit that was not kept, never below zero. |
| Two or more | No deduction under this rule. |

The discounted repair amount is the call's repair parts lines as billed plus its valued repair labor, after the tier's member repair discount percentage is taken off that sum once.

## Worked cases (hypothetical Comfort Club Platinum Plus call, 20% member repair discount)
Repair parts 400.00 and repair labor 300.00; discounted repair amount 560.00.

| Tune-ups kept | Working | Maintained repair amount |
|---|---|---|
| 0 | 400.00 less 20% | 320.00 |
| 1 | 560.00 less 109.00 | 451.00 |
| 2 | no deduction | 560.00 |

With exactly one tune-up and a discounted repair amount of only 80.00, the maintained repair amount is 0.00, since 80.00 less 109.00 would fall below zero.

## Points of judgement
- A heating tune-up 11 months before the date of handling and a cooling tune-up 13 months before: one counts, so the one-tune-up line applies.
- A whole-home visit does not count toward the tune-ups.
